properties.chose: One increment, as recommended. Anthony, 2026-10-05: "yes, do 1-3", to a list whose item read: "Build the VS Code setup as one increment: the accepted hooks (12) together with init installing the route and skill stubs (1, 7, 11)". His answer was relayed by the session that put the list to him, and is recorded as relayed. Idea 11, the CI probe, is the door test that step 5's requirement already asks for. The harness name (idea 8) was not named, and is not in this increment.
properties.decision:
WHAT IS DECIDED: step 5 of the door plan (epoch:planned-the-call-door-works-for-an-agent-that-cannot-use-mcp) is built as ONE increment. It holds four ideas of art:vscode-call-door-field-report-2026-10-02, in the report's words:
- idea 1: "A served CLI-door harness in `reflow2 init` (`--harness vscode-cli`): writes the instructions file into `.github/instructions/`, served from the binary so `reflow2 update` refreshes it, plus VS Code hook files (idea 12). Fixes 1, 9, 11."
- idea 7: "Skill stubs in `.github/skills/` that route to `get_skill`, so VS Code picks skills by description. Fixes 7."
- idea 11: "A CI probe for the door (`tools/test_call_door.py`, beside `test_opencode_plugin.py`)."
- idea 12, as accepted on 2026-10-02 in dec:idea-how-reflow2-triggers-the-loop-for-a-call-door-agent-in-vs-code: a SessionStart hook runs loop_status, a Stop hook exports and nudges, the nudge counts door writes, and any shipped command-line guard matches the executable position.

WHERE THESE IDEAS WERE ALREADY RECORDED, so this mints no second record of them. Ideas 1, 7 and 11 were brainstormed from the report's 2026-10-01 version (using_call.md) in dec:idea-the-call-door-becomes-a-supported-harness-for-an-agent-that-cannot-use-mcp, settled 2026-10-01, which left "which pieces land, and in what order" to the plan. Their MUSTs are in req:init-installs-the-terminal-route-for-vs-code-and-update-keeps-it-current. This decision is that order for these pieces.

NOT IN THIS INCREMENT:
- idea 8, a harness name for door calls. It is the requirement's attribution MUST (fact:root-cause-door-calls-carry-a-fixed-client-name-and-no-attribution-route-reaches-the-door-2026-10-02). The approval did not name it, so it stays in the requirement, unscheduled by this decision.
- idea 6, the batch door, stays step 6 (req:a-batch-of-calls-runs-under-one-approval-and-one-export).

SIZE: moderate.
- init and update gain a door harness entry and its files (instructions, skill stubs, hook files), served from the binary so update refreshes them.
- One Python probe drives the binary the way the installed instructions tell an agent to.
- The hook decision's "the nudge counts door writes" needs either command-text parsing or a marker the door leaves, and the second is a binary change.
- No schema change.

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, kept beside it:
- One increment ties the pieces that need no binary change (instructions, stubs, probe) to the hook piece that may need one. If counting door writes stalls, the rest waits with it; splitting would ship the instructions and stubs first.
- VS Code marks agent hooks Preview, and an organisation can switch hooks, skills or prompt files off. None of that is measured on the reporting machine (fact:root-cause-vs-code-reads-project-skills-and-slash-prompts-and-init-installs-neither-for-it-2026-10-02 says so).
- Every file init writes is one more that update must keep current, which is limitation 11's own lesson.
- Whether a door harness replaces the vscode MCP entry or sits beside it is still open (the L11 finding's point 9).
properties.name: ACCEPTED 2026-10-05 — the VS Code setup is built as one increment: init installs the door route and the skill stubs, CI drives the door as an agent does, and the hooks ship with them (report ideas 1, 7, 11 and 12)
properties.rationale:
Why one increment: ideas 1, 7 and 12 write files into the same project through one harness entry (.github/instructions, .github/skills, .github/hooks), and update must refresh all three, so building them apart would build that entry twice. Idea 11 is the test that keeps the installed text true through the door, the requirement's last MUST ("CI drives it the way an agent does").

The requirement stays proposed. This approval names three of its four MUSTs, and moving its status is the owner's own act.
